sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose of splitting shared benefit
sections.what: Explains that one shared capability should be divided among the processes that use it, rather than counted for each. It also sets the rounding precision for the shares.
sections.why: Stated in the docstring: counting one capability many times inflates the headline, and division by effort is arithmetic that belongs in code.
sections.watch_out: The rounding precision must stay small enough for shares to sum within the schema tolerance, or valid portfolios will fail validation.

sections.name: attribution_weights
sections.title: Splitting shared benefit by effort
sections.what: Gives each claiming process a share of one shared capability's benefit, in proportion to its baseline effort. If no process reports any effort, the shares are equal. The shares are rounded and the last one is adjusted so they add to exactly one.
sections.why: Stated in the docstring: a proportional rule is a decision that someone can disagree with, and equal shares when effort is zero avoid dropping the capability entirely.
sections.watch_out: The last name in the sorted list absorbs the rounding difference, so renaming a process can change who absorbs it.

sections.name: duplication_ratio
sections.title: Ratio showing how much double counting was removed
sections.what: Divides the gross total by the de-duplicated total. A value near one means the processes are independent, and larger values mean much was counted more than once. It raises an error if the de-duplicated total is zero or negative.
sections.why: Stated in the docstring: this is the first diagnostic shown when someone questions the headline figure.
sections.watch_out: The error stops the report, so any caller that expects zero to be a valid result will fail.

summary: Splits the benefit of one shared capability across the processes that claim it, in proportion to their effort, and measures how much double counting was removed.
purpose: Stops a shared capability's benefit being counted repeatedly, and gives a ratio that shows the gap between raw and de-duplicated totals.
why: Stated in the docstring: dividing one pool is arithmetic and belongs in code. Splitting evenly when no effort is reported keeps the capability from disappearing from the total.
how: Take each claimant's effort, sort the names, and compute each share as its fraction of the total. Round each share, then push any rounding remainder onto the last name so the shares add to exactly one. Separately, divide the gross total by the de-duplicated total to get the ratio.
inputs: A mapping of process name to effort, plus gross totals per process and the de-duplicated total.
outputs: A mapping of process name to share, which adds to one, and a single duplication ratio.
risks: Negative effort is treated as zero. A zero de-duplicated total raises an error. Renaming a process can change which process absorbs the rounding remainder.
debug: If shares do not add to one, check the rounding precision and that every process is in the mapping. If the ratio raises an error, check whether the de-duplicated total is zero because of bad input.
